Chalk and glass: what this site borrows from Reims and Paris

Two cities taught this site how to look: the chalk and the cathedral glass of Reims, the limestone and the gallery white of Paris.

Reims keeps its wine in chalk, deep cold galleries cut by hand, white that is never clinical. Above ground, the cathedral holds the blue of its windows against grey stone, and the blue is the first thing you remember. That is the palette here: chalk for the page, cobalt for the one thing that matters on it, a thread of gold because champagne is in the ground.

Paris gave me the way a gallery hangs a work: a small label, a number, and a lot of air. So the projects sit on a shelf as books you take down and open, each with its label and its number, each with air around it. Nothing shouts. The eye rests, then it finds the blue.

The symbol on the home page comes from the same place: a rose window built from cobalt glass petals around a chalk heart, with a gold ring, turning slowly in the light. I wanted something that could not have come from a template, the way a window in a cathedral could not.

This journal will also hold the landscapes and the small things around me that make me want to make things. They will arrive as I film them, in Maryland light, which is nothing like the light of Reims, and which I am learning to love anyway.
